takeaway: Carpal tunnel syndrome: compression of the median nerve beneath the transverse carpal ligament causes numbness, thenar atrophy and positive Tinel's and Phalen's signs.

lines.text: A 48-year-old woman has had numbness and tingling in her left hand for a year.
lines.say: A forty-eight-year-old woman has had numbness and tingling in her left hand for a year.

lines.text: It affects the radial three and a half digits, and her thenar eminence has wasted.
Tinel's sign is positive over her wrist,
and Phalen's sign is positive too.
Here, at the wrist, is the transverse carpal ligament.
Beneath it, the median nerve is compressed.
So compression of the median nerve causes her symptoms.
